text:
Ella (Support): Heads-up — ACME (via Tom) reports a burst of 429s on /v1/rerank starting ~2h ago. ~30% of requests back with 429, spike correlates with peak of search traffic.
Tom (Customer Success): customer says it's happening for both their sandbox and prod tokens. They pasted a couple of responses — header `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0` on a bunch of calls.
Ella (Support): sample error body they sent: `{"code":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"quota exceeded for route rerank-v1"}`
Maya (Eng-ML): ping @Sergio — could be per-route quota or a misconfigured token bucket for rerank. Any infra alerts?
Sergio (Eng-Infra): I don't see cluster-wide rate-limit alerts. I do see a sudden increase in connection rate to the rerank pool around +2h. Might be a traffic pattern shift in ACME. Any request examples?
Tom (Customer Success): sent request example: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME" \ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ \
  -d '{"query":"best rust web framework","candidates":["actix","rocket","axum","warp", ... up to 120 items]}'```
Ella (Support): they include candidate lists often >64, sometimes 120. Is rerank subject to per-request candidate limits + per-minute rate quotas?
Maya (Eng-ML): yes — two things: we have a per-request candidate cap (128) and a soft circuit for high-cardinality rerank requests that reduces throughput. Also we throttle by tokens-per-minute on rerank routes because it's heavy. If they simultaneously send many large candidate lists, they'll hit quota quickly.
Sergio (Eng-Infra): I pulled headers from our proxy logs for one of their tokens — `x-rate-limit-limit: 600`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 45` (s). So they're exhausting allowance. Their burstiness = many concurrent big requests.
Tom (Customer Success): customer says they had no code changes; traffic increase caused by an internal job that started iterating queries. They want a quick mitigation — either temporary quota bump or guidance.
Ella (Support): recommended immediate steps I sent to them: 1) exponentially backoff on 429 with jitter, 2) batch candidates smaller (<=32) where possible, 3) add client-side caching of rerank outputs for repeated queries, 4) if critical, request a support quota review.
Maya (Eng-ML): also recommend moving heavy rerank offline — run periodic background reranks and store scores in DB for serving, rather than per-user live when you have many candidates. For now we can offer a temporary token-level quota bump from infra if Org approves.
Sergio (Eng-Infra): I can provision a temporary bump scoped to their token for 60m. Need org name and justification. Also we should check whether our per-route rate-limiter has a bug where large payloads aren't charged proportionally (i.e., counting requests not candidate ops). If we're only counting requests, a 120-candidate request is much heavier than 1-candidate.
Maya (Eng-ML): right — our accounting currently charges per-request + a candidate multiplier, but there's a threshold where multiplier rounds down. I'll open a quick eval to see if that edge-case hit them.
Ella (Support): Tom — can you confirm if ACME wants a temp bump? They asked for immediate fix.
Tom (Customer Success): yes they accepted temp bump. I gave them best-effort mitigations; sending org approval now.
Sergio (Eng-Infra): done — bumped `sk-ACME` rerank quota +2x for 60 minutes. Watch logs for new drop in 429s.
rate-limiter-bot: alert cleared for token sk-ACME at 1945001301.
Tom (Customer Success): customer confirms fewer 429s but still occasional ones on largest candidate lists.
Maya (Eng-ML): ok still getting 429 on requests with >96 candidates. I'll run a quick simulation locally to reproduce shape. Possible fix: enforce stricter per-request candidate cost in billing meter and route to a higher-capacity pool when candidate_count>64.
Sergio (Eng-Infra): opened infra ticket INF-4721 to add stricter accounting and to create an autoscale rule for high-CPU rerank jobs.
Ella (Support): logging follow-up for the thread: 1) Customer got temp bump and mitigation steps. 2) Eng-ML investigating candidate multiplier edge. 3) Eng-Infra created INF-4721 for autoscale + billing accounting. 4) Recommend support to close once ACME confirms stable for 24h.
Tom (Customer Success): ACME appreciates the response. I'll keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
Maya (Eng-ML): quick repro note for posterity — sample payload that produced 429 in simulation: `{"query":"q","candidates":["a"...120],"top_k":10}`. Simulated cpu/time scaled ~3.8x vs 32 candidate job.
Sergio (Eng-Infra): I'll follow up in INF-4721 with logs and a proposal to route >64 candidate requests to a dedicated pool that has separate quotas.
Ella (Support): thanks everyone. If ACME sees regression, reopen thread.
Tom (Customer Success): closing loop for now — will report back in 24h. :white_check_mark:
